newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short synthetic position established in BT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short synthetic position established in BT.

text.p: A bearish deal in British Telecommunications was the largest deal in the UK stock options market by Tuesday afternoon, dealers said.

"The underlying shares have run up 26 percent since October and the threat of a windfall tax on BT from a Labour government if they win the general election may have been behind the deal," said one dealer.

It concerned buying 2,500 August 460 puts at 44p which was partly financed by selling 2,500 August 460 calls at 15p in a short synthetic sale. In general, if the shares fall the value of the puts will go up and a profit can be made.
But if the shares rally, the put premium will come down. And if the shares go above 460p there is a risk the calls will be assigned. By 1530 GMT, BT shares had gained 5-1/2p to 441-1/2p.
Over in Imperial Chemical Industries a diagonal ratio put spread was the main deal and it involved buying 505 April 800 puts at 90p and selling 541 July 750 puts at 48p.

Increased volatility of ICI shares will widen the spread sufficiently to make a profit by April expiry. After that, if the short puts are still held, ICI shares need to stay above 750p in order to make money.

In diversified industrials group Lonrho one trader bought 514 March 160 puts at 16p and sold 512 June 160 puts at 17p. Since the March puts expire tomorrow, this may have been the rolling forward of a short put position, dealers said.
Lonrho shares added a penny to 146p.
On Monday, Lonrho warned that its first-half profits "could be one third down on the previous year".
